headline: Overnight funding back at the 1.25% anchor; CGB 10Y hits a fresh 1-year low of 1.575%, long end leads
summary: CGBs rallied about 1–2bp across the curve as overnight funding eased after the tax period: the CCDC 10-year fell 1.4bp to 1.575%, another 1-year low, and the 30-year fell 1.4bp to 2.040%, with 20–50Y down 1.4–2.2bp while 1–2Y moved only 0.2–0.3bp. The long end led and 2s10s flattened to 34.8bp, a 1-year low. Policy banks kept pace at 10Y but lagged in the belly and front: CDB 10-year fell 0.9bp to 1.690%, widening its spread over CGB to 11.4bp, ADBC 10-year fell 1.2bp to 1.706%, and CDB 2Y rose 0.5bp.
drivers: Funding eases after the tax period

The PBOC added a net RMB67.3bn through RMB767.5bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25%, and the overnight Shibor fell 3.3bp to 1.26%, its lowest since May, with weighted overnight repo back near the 1.25% anchor. Wire wraps credited cheaper funding as the main reason sentiment improved.
Fund redemptions fade; real-money buying of duration

Funds that had been selling for two weeks have started buying long CGBs again and short-duration bond funds are seeing small inflows, per Shanghai Securities News. That helped TL futures gain 0.44% and pushed 20–50Y CGBs down 1.4–2.2bp, more than the 0.2–0.3bp at 1–2Y.

The Shanghai Composite fell 0.28% and the ChiNext 0.79%, with A-share turnover of about RMB1.31tn, the lowest this year, and over 4,800 stocks down. The soft equity tape supported bonds, while the Xi–Trump and trilateral talks in Shenzhen produced no market-moving economic news.
Policy banks keep pace at 10Y; tax overhang remains

ADBC reopened 10-year and 5-year bonds at 1.718% and 1.469%, close to secondary levels, and CDB 10Y fell 0.9bp, slightly less than CGBs. Brokers still see the bond-interest tax debate capping the CDB–CGB 10Y spread compression, so the spread widened 0.5bp to 11.4bp.
data: +RMB39.5bn to RMB2.08tn; sixth monthly rise, largest since May
Steady haven buying supports CGBs over policy banks and helps the strong yuan.
Industrial output 4.8% y/y (f 5.3%, p 5.5%); retail sales 0.4% (f 0.8%, p 1.1%); FAI YTD −8.1% (f −7.0%, p −7.2%); property investment −21.6%
Broad miss with collapsing investment supports lower yields and the case for more fiscal and monetary support.
Smallest annual fall in 11 months but monthly declines persist, so no lift to credit demand yet.
New loans −RMB100bn (f +RMB20bn, p +RMB1.08tn); TSF RMB1.15tn (f 1.42tn, p 3.55tn); M2 7.1% (f 7.2–7.3%, p 7.2%); M1 4.4% (p 3.2%)
Record-low 4.7% loan growth confirms weak private demand and supports lower yields.
Strong external demand trims the growth-scare case for bonds and triggered mild profit-taking.
Soft household demand keeps the easing bias intact and supports low long-end yields.
Energy-driven cost push that squeezes margins rather than signalling demand; bonds looked through it.
view: Neutral with a mild bullish lean for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.55–1.61% CCDC range. The 10-year long from 1.628% reached the 1.58% target today (1.575%, 0th percentile of the year), so I take profit and would only re-buy on a back-up toward 1.61–1.62%; overnight funding at the 1.25% anchor, fading redemptions and weak equities support bonds, but at 1-year lows the payoff is thin and the hawkish Fed and dollar strength limit room for a deeper PBOC move. On the curve I prefer to pick up spread rather than duration: CDB 7Y at 19bp over CGB and CDB 10Y near 12bp are where value is building, while the CGB belly stays rich. A renewed redemption wave, a formal bond-interest tax plan or DR001 back above 1.35% would push the 10-year to 1.62%; an LPR cut on Friday or a weak November PMI would take it toward 1.55%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year eased 0.2bp to 1.228% (5th percentile, average 1.299%) and the 1-year 0.3bp to 1.173%, lagging the long end. Overnight funding back near the 1.25% policy rate helps carry, but at 1.23% the 2-year offers only about 2bp over the anchor, so I do not chase.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if DR001 settles below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp hit its 25bp target, closing at 24.9bp (27th percentile, average 26.7bp), so I take profit. The belly stays rich: 2s5s10s is −15.1bp (10th percentile, average −8.1bp) with the 5-year at 1.326%, but after a 4bp move the flattener's edge is used up.
buckets.call: Take profit on the 5s10s flattener at 24.9bp; re-enter at 28bp or wider, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year fell 1.4bp to 1.575%, a fresh 1-year low (0th percentile, average 1.752%) and 6.6bp lower over a month, so the long from 1.628% hit its 1.58% target. Against neighbours it is fair (7s10s20s −30.0bp, 45th percentile), but the outright level is the year's richest.
buckets.call: Take profit on the 10-year long at ~1.575%; re-buy at 1.61–1.62%, target 1.57%, stop 1.65%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year fell 1.4bp to 2.040% (1st percentile, average 2.213%) and TL futures gained 0.44% as funds returned to the long end; 10s30s held at 46.5bp (51st percentile, average 46.1bp). 30s50s is 10.3bp (3rd percentile), so 50Y is the richest point; insurer year-end demand should cap 30Y near 2.10%.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~48bp); poor risk/reward below 2.02%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: The CDB 10-year spread over CGB widened 0.5bp to 11.4bp (62nd percentile, average 9.6bp), now 0.6bp from the 12bp entry, as CDB lagged the CGB rally. At 1–2Y policy banks remain near 1-year tights (CDB 2Y 12.1bp, 5th percentile), so value is only at 7–10Y.
buckets.call: Buy CDB 10Y vs CGB 10Y at 12bp or wider, target 9bp, stop 15bp; avoid 1–3Y policy banks.

buckets.name: Policy banks 5–7Y vs CGB
buckets.why: The CDB 7-year spread over CGB is 19.3bp (72nd percentile, average 15.8bp) and ADBC 7Y 18.7bp (96th percentile), both little changed. The tax repricing keeps the tenor cheap, and fading fund redemptions are a first step, but I still want a wider entry before re-engaging.
buckets.call: Flat; re-enter CDB 7Y vs CGB 7Y at 23bp+, target 18bp, stop 26bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 1.6bp more than CDB (57th percentile, average 1.4bp), 0.4bp less than Wednesday as ADBC outperformed; EXIM is 1.1bp (13th percentile, average 2.0bp). ADBC's 10-year reopening cleared at 1.718%, near secondary, so supply is being absorbed.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC 10Y over CDB 10Y; switch back to CDB if the pickup falls below 1bp. Avoid EXIM 10Y at about 1bp.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: The CDB 20-year spread over CGB is 10.1bp (55th percentile, average 10.3bp), as both curves fell 1.4–1.6bp. The CDB 30-year spread is 11.0bp, still a 1-year tight (average 12.5bp), so long policy banks offer no value against CGBs.
buckets.call: Flat; re-enter CGB 20Y over CDB 20Y below 7bp; avoid CDB 30Y at an 11bp spread.

watch: Next: the November LPR and a 30-year CGB reopening (Nov 20), an RMB80bn 10-year CGB reopening (Nov 24), October industrial profits (Nov 27), November official PMIs (Nov 30), daily PBOC overnight operations at 1.25% and month-end funding, fund redemption data, any official word on bond interest tax, and US data ahead of the December FOMC, where markets now price a hike.
